School & learning

syllable noun

also syllables

classical

Quint. 9.4.61: neque enim loquī possumus nisi syllabīs brevibus ac longīs
Cic. Par. 26: syllaba brevior aut longior (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 237, 249

syllaba, syllabae f.

noun, first declension

a syllable

Letters make syllables and syllables make words: litterae faciunt syllabās, syllabae faciunt dictiōnēs (Traupman 247, 249). On which syllable the stress falls: In quā syllabā accentum pōnimus? (Traupman 237).

Examples

  • neque enim loquī possumus nisi syllabīs brevibus ac longīs, ex quibus pedēs fīunt

    for we cannot speak except in short and long syllables, from which feet are madeQuint. 9.4.61

See also vowel, consonant, penult, antepenult, last syllable, stress, long.
